correctness.rationale: Every admissible table is represented exactly by two positive four-part compositions of the common arm size. The strict within-stratum and pooled inequalities are tested by exact integer cross products. Exhaustive enumeration gives zero reversals through arm size 10 and four at arm size 11; direct replay verifies both symmetry orbits and the pooled association sign.

originality.rationale: Prior work covers Simpson reversal broadly and gives balanced examples, while a public challenge asks an adjacent unconstrained minimum problem. No inspected source states the equal-pooled-arm, all-positive-cell minimum of 11 per arm or the exact two-orbit first layer.
residual_risks: The archived Brilliant challenge is a close adjacent minimum problem; an unindexed solution could also discuss the balanced positive-cell specialization.
The full Samuels 1993 article was not available through the checked route; its abstract describing necessary and sufficient reversal conditions was inspected.
Different domains—zero cells, unequal pooled group totals, more than two strata, or weak rather than strict inequalities—have different minima.

value.rationale: Simpson reversal is a canonical warning in epidemiology and experimental interpretation. Equal total arm sizes are common in comparative designs, while positive cells exclude degenerate rate comparisons. The theorem identifies the smallest fully nondegenerate balanced dataset that can still reverse every stratum-specific direction, and its complete first layer provides a compact stress-test set for teaching and software.
